question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Dutch Arrival in India — Year and Port]
options: First Dutch fleet to India — 1595–1597, Cornelis de Houtman to Banten (Java)
Dutch first factory in India established — Masulipatnam on Coromandel Coast
Dutch first arrived in India via — Cape of Good Hope to Calicut (1498)
wrong_fact: Arriving via the Cape of Good Hope to Calicut in 1498 describes Vasco da Gama's voyage for Portugal, NOT the Dutch. The Dutch arrived much later — their first fleet reached Banten (Java) in 1595–97, not Calicut in 1498.
explanation: The Dutch first voyage to Asia under Cornelis de Houtman reached Banten, Java in 1595–97. The Dutch established their first factory in India at Masulipatnam on the Coromandel Coast in 1605. Arriving at Calicut via Cape of Good Hope in 1498 is the description of Vasco da Gama's Portuguese voyage, not the Dutch.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Dutch settlements in India — Location and Coast]
options: Pulicat — Coromandel Coast, north of Madras
wrong_fact: Cochin (Kochi) is located on the Malabar (West) Coast of Kerala, NOT on the Coromandel Coast. The Coromandel Coast faces the Bay of Bengal on the eastern side of peninsular India.
explanation: Masulipatnam, Pulicat, and Nagapattinam are all correctly located on the Coromandel (Eastern) Coast. Cochin/Kochi, however, is on the Malabar (Western) Coast of Kerala, facing the Arabian Sea. Confusing east and west coasts is a classic exam trap.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Dutch expansion in India — Governor/Admiral and Event]
options: Cornelis de Houtman — led first Dutch fleet to Asia (1595)
Jan Pieterszoon Coen — established Batavia as VOC headquarters (1619)
Rijklof van Goens — Dutch commander who attacked Portuguese positions in India and Ceylon
Pieter Both — Dutch governor who defeated Travancore at Battle of Colachel
wrong_fact: The Battle of Colachel (1741) resulted in a Dutch DEFEAT by Travancore under Marthanda Varma — the Dutch did not win it. Pieter Both was the first Governor-General of Dutch East Indies (1610–1614), not related to Colachel.
explanation: Cornelis de Houtman led the first Dutch fleet to Asia in 1595. Jan Pieterszoon Coen founded Batavia in 1619. Rijklof van Goens was a VOC commander who led campaigns in India and Ceylon. However, Pieter Both did not win at Colachel — the Dutch were decisively defeated there by Travancore's forces in 1741, marking the end of Dutch power in India.
